ce:2012:q1.question: The estimate of $\int_{0.5}^{0.5}\frac{dx}{x}$ obtained using Simpson's rule with three-point function evaluation exceeds the exact value by

detailed_solution.markdown: Exact value of $\int_{0.5}^{1.5}\frac{dx}{x}=\left [ \log x \right ]_{0.5}^{1.5} = \log (1.5)- \log(0.5) =1.0986$ Approximate value by Simpson's rule with 3 point is, $$\begin{aligned} I&=\frac{h}{3}\left ( f\left ( 0 \right )+4f\left ( 1 \right )+f\left ( 2 \right ) \right ) \\ n_{i}&=n_{pt}-1=3-1=2 \end{aligned}$$ ($n_{pt}$ is the number of pts and $n_{i}$ is the number of intervals) Here $h=\frac{b-a}{n_{i}}=\frac{1.5-0.5}{2}=0.5$ The table is $I=\frac{0.5}{3}\left ( \frac{1}{0.5}+4 \times 1+\frac{1}{1.5}\right ) = 1.1111$ So the estimate exceeds the exact value by, Approximate value-Exact value $=0.012499 \approx 0.012499$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

which is $\lt 50\%$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2012:q26.question: The error in $\frac{d}{dx}f(x)|_{x=x_{0}}$ for a continuous function estimated with h = 0.03 using the central difference formula $\frac{d}{dx}f(x)|_{x=x_{0}}\approx \frac{f(x_{0}+h)-f(x_{0}-h)}{2h}, \text{ is } 2 \times 10^{-3}$. ce:2012:q29.title: GATE CE 2012 | Set 1 | Question: 29
ce:2012:q29.question: For the parallelogram OPQR shown in the sketch, $\overrightarrow{OP}=a\hat{i}+b\hat{j} \; and \; \overrightarrow{OR}=c\hat{i}+d\hat{j}$. The area of the parallelogram is

detailed_solution.markdown: The area of parallelogram OPQR in figure shown above, is the magnitude of the vector product $$\begin{aligned} &=\left | \overrightarrow{OP}\times \overrightarrow{OR} \right | \\ \overrightarrow{OP}&=a\hat{i}+b\hat{j} \\ \overrightarrow{OR}&=c\hat{i}+d\hat{j} \\ \overrightarrow{OP}\times \overrightarrow{OR}&=\begin{vmatrix} i & j & k\\ a & b & 0\\ c & d & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\ &=0\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+\left ( ad-bc \right )\hat{k} \\ \left | \overrightarrow{OP}\times \overrightarrow{OR} \right |&=\sqrt{0^{2}+0^{2}+\left ( ad-bc \right )^{2}} \\ &=ad-bc \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2012:q30.question: The solution of the ordinary differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=0$ for the boundary condition, y = 5 at x = 1 is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Given, }\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+2y&=0 \text{ and } y(1)=5 \\    \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}&=-2y \\    \int \frac{dy}{y}&=\int -2dx \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  \ln y&=-2x+c \\ \Rightarrow   \;\; y&=e^{-2x}.e^{c}=c_{1}e^{-2x} \\    y\left ( 1 \right )&=c_{1}e^{-2}=5 \\ \Rightarrow \; c_{1}&=\frac{5}{e^{-2}} \\ \text{So, }   y&=\frac{5}{e^{-2}}e^{-2x}=5e^{2}e^{-2x} \\     &=36.95\, e^{-2x} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2012:q33.title: GATE CE 2012 | Set 1 | Question: 33

detailed_solution.markdown: $\text { Total stress at Bottom }=\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P_{\theta}}{I} y-\frac{M}{Z}$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { Here, } Z &=\frac{b d^{2}}{6}=\frac{500 \times 750^{2}}{6} \\ &=46.875 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{mm}^{3} \\ e &=145 \mathrm{mm} ; P=1620 \mathrm{kN} \\ M &=\frac{w l^{2}}{8}=\frac{45 \times 7.3^{2}}{8}=299.76 \mathrm{kNm} \\ \therefore \frac{P}{A} &=\frac{1620 \times 10^{3}}{500 \times 750}=4.32 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ \frac{P e}{Z} &=\frac{1620 \times 10^{3} \times 145}{46.875 \times 10^{6}}=5.01 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ \frac{M}{Z}&=\frac{299.76 \times 10^{6}}{46.875 \times 10^{6}} =6.39 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ \therefore &\text { Total stress at bottom } =4.32+5.01-6.39 \\ &=2.94 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} . \text { (comp.) } \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2012:q35.title: GATE CE 2012 | Set 1 | Question: 35
ce:2012:q35.question: Two plates are connected by fillet welds of size 10 mm and subjected to tension, as shown in the sketch. The thickness of each plate is 12 mm. detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Structural Fasteners
detailed_solution.markdown: Maximum force transmitted by plate $=P$ $P=A_{g}\times \frac{f_{y}}{1.1}= \left ( 12\times 100 \right )\times \frac{250}{1.1} =272.72 kN$ Force resisted by weld, $P=272.72 kN \;\;\;...(i)$ Let length of weld on either side $=l$ Size of weld (S)=10 mm Force resisted by weld $=\frac{0.7\times S}{1.25}\times \left ( \frac{f_{u}}{\sqrt{3}}\right )\times l$ Size = 10 mm Throat thickness $=0.7\times 10= 7 mm$ $=\frac{7\times 410}{1.25\times \sqrt{3}}\times l \;\;\;...(ii)$ From equations(i) and (ii), $272.72\times 10^{3}=\frac{7\times 410}{1.25\times \sqrt{3}\times l}$ $l=205.8$ mm Length eq. of each side$=\frac{l}{2}= 103 mm\simeq 105 mm$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2012:q36.title: GATE CE 2012 | Set 1 | Question: 36
ce:2012:q36.question:
Two soil specimens with identical geometric dimensions were subjected to falling head
permeability tests in the laboratory under identical conditions. The fall of water head was measured
after an identical time interval. The ratio of initial to final water heads for the test involving the first
specimen was 1.25. If the coefficient of permeability of the second specimen is 5-times that of the
first, the ratio of initial to final water heads in the test involving the second specimen is

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, For first specimen.

$\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}=1.25 \; \& \; k_{2}=5 k_{1}$

then for second specimen, $\frac{h'_1}{h'_2}=?$

We know that; for falling head permeability test.

$$\begin{aligned} k&=\frac{2.303 a L}{A \cdot t} \log _{10}\left(\frac{h_{1}}{h_{2}}\right)\\ \therefore \quad \frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}&=\frac{\log _{10}\left(h'_{1} / h'_{2}\right)}{\log _{10}\left(h_{1} / h_{2}\right)} \\ \Rightarrow 5 \log _{10} 1.25&=\log _{10}\left(\frac{h'_{1}}{h'_{2}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{h'_{1}}{h'_{2}}&=3.05 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

$$\begin{aligned} \Delta \bar{\sigma} &=20 \mathrm{kPa}, \bar{\sigma}_{0}=100 \mathrm{kPa} \\ G &=2.7 \\ \mathrm{w} &=45 \% \\ \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}} &=0.45 \\ \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}} &=0.05 \\ \mathrm{H}_{0} &=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \therefore \quad \Delta \mathrm{H} &=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{H}_{0}}{1+\mathrm{e}_{0}} \log _{10}\left[\frac{\overline{\mathrm{\sigma}}_{0}+\Delta \overline{\mathrm{o}}}{\overline{\mathrm{\sigma}}_{0}}\right] \\ \text{Also},\quad wG&=eS \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.45 \times 2.7 &=e .1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad &=1.215 \\ \therefore \quad \Delta H &=\frac{0.45 \times 1}{1+1.215} \log _{10}\left(\frac{(100+20)}{100}\right) \\ &=\frac{0.45}{2.215} \log _{10}\left(\frac{120}{100}\right) \\ &=0.016 \mathrm{m}=16 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2012:q45.question:

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{ccc} \text{Length of curve,} &L_{c}&=200 \mathrm{m} \\ \text{ Radius,}&R&=300 \mathrm{m}\\ \text{Width,}&w&=7.5 \mathrm{m}\\ \text{SSD, }&S&=80 \mathrm{m} \\ \because \quad L_{c} \gt S&& \end{array}$$

Set back distance,

$$\begin{aligned} m &=(R)-(R-d) \cos \frac{\alpha}{2} \\ \frac{\alpha}{2} &=\frac{180 \cdot S}{2 \pi(R-d)}=\frac{180 \times 80}{2 \pi \times\left(300-\frac{7.5}{4}\right)} \\ &=7.687 \\ m &=300-\left(300-\frac{7.5}{4}\right) \cos (7.687) \\ &=2.67 \end{aligned}$$

After this: The setback distance (in m) required from the centre line of the inner lane of the pavement is $= 4.55-\frac{7.5}{4} = 2.675 m$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.
